newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish C.Bank sees 96 GNP at 6.0pct, 5.0pct in 97.
newsitem.headline: Irish C.Bank sees 96 GNP at 6.0pct, 5.0pct in 97.

text.p: Ireland's Central Bank said on Wednesday that it expects GNP to grow at 6.0 percent in 1996 followed by a modest deceleration to 5.0 pct in 1997.
The Central Bank said in its quarterly bulletin that inflation for the year as a whole is now expected to average 1.7 percent.
Following three years of very strong growth, however, some pick-up in inflation is expected, it warned.
"On the basis of current indicators, some upward pressure on prices is expected in 1997 with the rate of consumer price inflation forecast to rise to 2.3 percent," the central bank said.

It said during 1996, a sustained increase in consumer spending was supported by strong growth in disposable incomes. In volume terms, it expected consumption to grow by 6.0 percent but decelerate to 4.0 percent in 1997.
It said export growth was also reasonably strong in 1996 but noticeably weaker than in 1995. Against this, imports grew strongly reflecting the growth in domestic demand, it said.
The current account surplus is expected to decline to 1.25 percent of GNP in 1996 but rise to 2.0 percent in 1997, it said.
It expected a significant undershoot in the government budget target for the Exchequer Borrowing Requirement (EBR) in 1996. The government set a target 1996 EBR at 729 million Irish pounds.

The central bank said this opened up the prospect of significant tax reform but warned that it was important to ensure that, at a time when the economy was performing strongly, fiscal policy should not be expansionary.
In the labour market, it said, there was evidence of further employment growth in 1996.

In the year to mid-April, Labour Force Survey estimates indicate that total numbers at work rose by 45,000 but as a result of significant labour force growth, the central bank said it expected only a modest drop in the unemployment rate to 12.25 percent.
"The outlook for 1997 is for further employment growth of 34,000 and a reduction in the unemployment rate to 11.75 percent," the bank said.
